context: Checkpoint 2026-08-03 (phase 13 opens). Two field defects came back from real Termux use and both were measured rather than guessed. The select prompt reprinted itself on every keypress: `renderedLines` counted logical lines while `moveCursor` climbs physical rows, so a wrapped option made the redraw rise short and leave everything above it — the same family as the secret mask, fixed and republished. The second is deeper and NOT a text problem: the wizard read as coupled to Telegram because (a) with one registered adapter the code selects it in silence, never saying it is a registry, and (b) the operator channel has no way to announce at all, so the preflight framing never left the node. That second half is the next slice. Earlier in the session the declared-node-base work closed completely (SOVEREIGN_BASE across seven sites, the node publishing node-descriptor.v1 with its pid, the auth policy defaulting to the node's own, and doctor naming the directory when they diverge). The operator's own framing of the convergence is worth keeping: the moment meta-work separates from work is not a state of refarm but a COST CURVE — declaring the first operation cost ~15 refarm fixes; when the Nth costs zero, it has arrived, and that is countable rather than felt.

next_actions: NEXT SLICE — the announcement contract. An operator channel carries QUESTIONS only: there is no notice/announce in prompt-contract-v1. So a wizard's framing never reaches a remote attender — `delivery add`'s preflight ("the bot is yours; refarm does not talk to BotFather for you") stayed on the node while only the questions travelled, and the operator read the result as a Telegram feature rather than one adapter in a registry. Every future wizard and every future surface inherits that muteness, so this precedes Telegram-as-surface and the PWA rather than following them. `stream:v1` already carries `notice` frames — check whether the operator channel should project that rather than grow a second vocabulary.

Ocamento as the operator reframed it (better than the earlier framing): do not 'declare operations' — position rcdc5 and vault-seed as CONSUMERS of refarm-as-framework, so each gets its own CLI and compatibility, declares installable operations, and reports DX pain back here. The direction inverts: the repo adopts refarm and complains, rather than refarm reaching into the repo. The complaint is the instrument — real pain, not simulated. vault-seed is the proven case (~12 blocks consumed); rcdc5 is mid-way.

Then Telegram as an operation surface, then the PWA companion — and the PWA deserves a design pass first: what is OF ITS OWN NATURE (offline, history, a consolidated view across several operations) rather than `/attend` with an icon. Note `/attend` is already complete for catalog+start+status+prompts over HTTPS at <tailnet>:4322/attend; the installable-PWA gap is home-screen, offline and push, not capability.
open_questions: Settled 2026-08-03: notices cross to the node by their OWN route (POST /notices), not as a field of POST /prompts. Riding the publish would make TRANSPORT inherit a DELIVERY rule (D9) that only coincides while the sole producer is a wizard that always asks next — and would leave every future node→operator statement (the VPN is up, an automation result, operation progress) needing a road of its own. That is the fragmentation D2 already documented across stream:v1, connection_frames and login-flow; this would have been the fourth. Auth is not a new decision: publishing is the asker's side, so like POST /prompts it is NOT reachable by a prompt:answer credential.

DESIGN ITEM (operator, 2026-08-03) — the respond/effort budget must be DECLARED PER DISPATCH, not read once at boot. `RespondWatchConfig { timeout_ms, interval_ms }` resolves at `SidecarState::new` from `REFARM_RESPOND_WATCH_TIMEOUT_MS` and `dispatch.rs:703` reads it as a process global, so raising it needs a runtime restart — the knob is out of reach exactly when you discover you need it. The PROMPT path already got this right in the same file: `PublishPromptRequest.timeout_ms` lets the asker declare its own deadline and the node merely CLAMPS it. Same decision, taken twice, right on one side and wrong on the other. The operator's framing: this granularity has to be controllable at runtime to allow SOVEREIGN SPAWN — whoever spawns work declares its budget rather than inheriting a centrally-configured one — because policies and loop engineering vary, and a boot-read global binds the system to one shape. A default still makes sense, as a default and as a ceiling, which is the role it already plays for prompts. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: the refarm agent died at steps 4/25 and 6/25 of a real investigation on the 45s ceiling while using the right tools; the budget was sized for the agent to REPLY, not to INVESTIGATE.
